title: Modernize GPU stack: CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS upgrades and kernel compatibility fixes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Our serving runtime uses a custom chain of GPU dependencies (CUDA, Triton, CUTLASS and a small set of custom kernels). Several internal and third-party workloads are failing or showing performance regressions with the older stack (CUDA 11.8 + Triton 2.0), and upstreams have released important bugfixes and performance improvements in CUDA 12.x, Triton 2.2+, and CUTLASS 2.x. This ticket is to coordinate a safe upgrade path and cleanup of kernel compatibility code.
scope: 1) Upgrade CI/build images to CUDA 12.1 and NVCC toolchain; 2) Upgrade Triton to 2.2 and CUTLASS to 2.x; 3) Audit and refactor custom GPU kernels that access shared memory / warp reductions; 4) Add compatibility shims for mixed-precision kernels; 5) Expand CI matrix to include new driver versions and a canary deploy for Dedicated clusters.
proposal: Phase 1: bump base images and run full integration on internal nightly models. Phase 2: identify failing kernels and refactor to modernized CUTLASS APIs (replace manual block reductions, align memory access, use tensor core dispatch helpers). Phase 3: run regression tests + perf benchmarks, roll out canary to 5% Dedicated capacity, monitor telemetry, then full rollout.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: subtle numerical differences in float16 path causing hallucination/regression for sensitive eval prompts. Mitigation: run existing eval suites (production prompts) and compare token-level divergences; add automatic regression alerting that blocks rollout if divergence > threshold. Risk: new Triton backend changes break older pinned model variants. Mitigation: maintain a fallback path to previous runtime binary for pinned customers and add automatic routing to fallback if canary fails.
testing_plan:
- Expand CI matrices to include (CUDA 11.8, CUDA 12.1) and (Triton 2.0, Triton 2.2).
- Run full unit, integration, and end-to-end generation tests on sample models (gpt-medium, gpt-large).
- Run production prompt eval suite (1000 prompts) and compare quality/regression metrics.
- Performance microbenchmarks: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, GPU util and memory.
- Canary: route 5% of Dedicated traffic for 48h, collect SLA and output-diff metrics.
acceptance_criteria: All CI green across new matrices
No customer-facing quality regression discovered in eval suite (token-level divergence <= 0.5% on weighted prompts)
Latency p50/p95 within 5% of baseline for primary models
Canary stable for 48h with error rate <= baseline + 0.1%
notes: We intentionally avoid changing model weights or tokenization. The goal is compatibility and perf. Patch CUTLASS usage only where it reduces complexity. Coordinate with infra for driver updates in Dedicated clusters.
